classes.title: VRAM/OOM failure
classes.birth_relevance: Operator training failure class (class-kill law, 2026-07-21): the 3B model must not OOM under the governed resource envelope; an unguarded OOM invalidates any training run silently.
classes.evidence: scripts/ember_01_custody/resource_dispatch_guard.py:check_vram_headroom -- fail-closed pre-dispatch VRAM assert reusing the same GOVERNOR_FLOOR pair src/ember/governance/scripts/v0_config_check.py already applies to config values (vram_fraction<=0.80, margin_gib_floor>=1.5 GiB), applied here to a LIVE counter reading (torch.cuda.mem_get_info() via read_vram_live()) BEFORE work starts instead of a static config check. Regression suite tests/ember_01_custody/test_resource_dispatch_guard.py (27 tests, no GPU allocation, fixture-driven): correctness (fraction-cap and margin-floor both proven to block independently), fail-closed on malformed/missing/negative/non-numeric readings, and a mutation-proof test (test_vram_headroom_mutation_guard_is_load_bearing) showing the guard's pass/fail is load-bearing -- an over-cap reading is correctly blocked with the guard present, and would be wrongly approved if the guard's check were stubbed to a no-op.

classes.evidence: scripts/ember_01_custody/resource_dispatch_guard.py:check_commit_charge_margin -- fail-closed pre-dispatch commit-charge assert applying the SAME 6GiB free-commit floor law as the in-run commit governor (visible-window-hygiene.md: 'margin < 6GB free commit at any phase boundary -> checkpoint + clean abort'; scripts/build_fixed_prior_manifest.py HOST_GOVERNOR_FLOOR_BYTES) pre-dispatch instead of mid-run, reading the same GlobalMemoryStatusEx.ullAvailPageFile counter as scripts/cbase_grow_rung2_gpu_offload_probe.py's _va_report / scripts/cbase_grow_rung2_event.py's phase_preflight (via read_commit_charge_live()). Regression suite tests/ember_01_custody/test_resource_dispatch_guard.py (same file, no host commit-charge draining, fixture-driven): correctness (below-floor blocks, at-floor passes), fail-closed on malformed/missing/negative/non-numeric readings, and a mutation-proof test (test_commit_charge_mutation_guard_is_load_bearing) showing a below-floor reading is correctly blocked with the guard present and would be wrongly approved if stubbed to a no-op.

classes.title: Native crash / segfault in the training loop
classes.birth_relevance: Operator training failure class (class-kill law, 2026-07-21): an unrecoverable native process death mid-run invalidates the run and, without a crash-survival guard, silently loses training state.
classes.evidence: scripts/ember_01_custody/native_crash_guard.py:run_supervised -- a supervised-dispatch wrapper: the risky work runs as a CHILD process, the parent classifies the exit code via classify_exit() (POSIX: negative returncode == -signal_number, e.g. SIGSEGV=-11; Windows: NTSTATUS fault-severity codes, mask 0xC0000000, e.g. STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION=0xC0000005 -- both representations verified empirically against this host, not assumed) and, on a detected crash, writes a fail-closed receipt (class, cmd, returncode, crash_signature, ts) to disk BEFORE returning, so no caller can make a relaunch decision before the crash is recorded. Regression suite tests/ember_01_custody/test_native_crash_guard.py (19 tests): classify_exit() correctness for both platform branches with hand-picked codes (host-OS-independent, parametrized), fail-closed on non-int input, run_supervised() proven against a REAL crashing child process (os.kill(SIGSEGV) on POSIX / ctypes ExitProcess(NTSTATUS) on Windows -- not a fabricated returncode) writing a receipt that passes src/ember/governance/scripts/receipt_check.py, and a mutation-proof test (test_run_supervised_mutation_guard_is_load_bearing) showing the same real crashing child is wrongly reported crashed=False with no receipt if classify_exit is stubbed to a no-op.

classes.title: BF16 silent gradient freeze
classes.birth_relevance: Operator training failure class (class-kill law, 2026-07-21): undetected gradient/loss saturation under BF16 produces a run that LOOKS like it trained but never learned, invalidating any completion claim.
classes.evidence: Reopened per the row's own bar: 'a LIVE guard on the current bf16-momentum path lands and is proven collectable + RED-first'. scripts/preflight/update_survival.py (landed #1232, merged 2026-07-31, independent of and postdating the dead #792 guard) is that live guard -- run_update_survival_preflight() distinguishes gradient-caused parameter movement from weight-decay movement under a treatment dtype (including bf16) and reports PREFLIGHT_FAIL when a tensor class's causal_changed_fraction falls below its declared survival floor, which is exactly the silent-freeze signature (parameters move under bf16 storage because of decay, not because the gradient actually updated them). Wired into C0 custody via tests/ember_01_custody/test_bf16_silent_freeze_guard_wiring.py (3 tests, collectable + green -- confirmed directly, not assumed): RED-first on the module's own BitNet 15-of-24 bf16 fixture (9 norm_scale tensors carry a gradient too small to clear their causal-survival floor -- a genuine silent freeze) rejected PREFLIGHT_FAIL; an isolated re-run with the per-tensor frozen_required_tensors path disabled proves the causal_changed_fraction class-floor path alone still catches the freeze; and a mutation-proof test (test_bf16_momentum_freeze_mutation_guard_is_load_bearing) showing the same fixture is wrongly accepted PREFLIGHT_PASS when the floor comparison is neutralized. #1232's own focused suite (tests/test_update_survival_preflight.py + 3 companion files, 16 tests) independently confirmed collectable and green on this checkout.

classes.title: Governed-abort observability loss
classes.birth_relevance: Operator training failure class (class-kill law, 2026-07-21): a governed abort (resource cap, headroom violation, kill-discipline stop) that leaves no receipt is indistinguishable from an unexplained hang, masking the real defect from post-mortem review.
classes.evidence: scripts/ember_01_custody/governed_abort_observability_guard.py:verify_abort_observed -- generalizes kill-discipline's 'receipt first' law (infra/vigil/kill-receipts.jsonl) to any governed training abort. emit_abort_receipt() is the mandatory call every governed-abort site (resource cap trip, headroom violation, phase-boundary commit-charge breach) must make BEFORE the abort completes, writing a structured receipt naming the trigger, thresholds, live_reading, and phase (build_abort_receipt() refuses to construct a receipt missing any of the four, fail-closed). verify_abort_observed(event, receipts_dir) fail-closed-checks that a matching receipt exists for a DETECTED abort event; no matching receipt is RED -- exactly the silent-abort failure this class names. Regression suite tests/ember_01_custody/test_governed_abort_observability_guard.py (21 tests): construction fail-closed on missing trigger/thresholds/live_reading/phase, checked-write emission (receipt passes src/ember/governance/scripts/receipt_check.py), detection correctness (trigger match, ts-window match, malformed-window/missing-dir/malformed-JSON-receipt all fail closed without raising), and a mutation-proof test (test_governed_abort_mutation_guard_is_load_bearing) showing a genuinely silent (unreceipted) abort event is wrongly approved if verify_abort_observed is stubbed to a no-op.

classes.title: Crash-survival / checkpoint validity across a crash
classes.birth_relevance: Operator training failure class (class-kill law, 2026-07-21): resuming from a checkpoint whose validity across a crash was never verified can silently continue training on corrupted state.
classes.evidence: scripts/ember_01_custody/crash_survival_guard.py:resume_guard -- the named-missing synthetic-crash resume probe, built on top of the existing checkpoint save/load identity binding (scripts/ember_01_identity/checkpoint_save_load_identity_binding.py:measure_checkpoint_identity, reused directly, never reimplemented) rather than a new identity mechanism. simulate_mid_crash_write() produces a genuine mid-crash artifact: a real torch checkpoint (multi-tensor, saved with torch.save) truncated to a fraction of its original byte length -- exactly what a process killed mid-fwrite (OOM-kill, native crash, power loss) leaves on disk. resume_guard() attempts to measure the shard via the trusted binding path and returns REJECTED (never an uncaught exception a caller could skip past) when the shard cannot be safely measured -- the shape a truncated write always takes. Regression suite tests/ember_01_custody/test_crash_survival_guard.py (11 tests, zero real Ember checkpoints, zero GPU): a complete checkpoint is ACCEPTED; truncation at 0%/10%/50%/90%/99% of the original length is REJECTED in every case; a missing checkpoint path is REJECTED as a resume-time verdict, not an exception; simulate_mid_crash_write fails closed on an out-of-range truncate_fraction; CLI exit-code parity; and a mutation-proof test (test_resume_guard_mutation_guard_is_load_bearing) showing the same mid-crash-truncated checkpoint is wrongly ACCEPTED if the fail-closed except clause is neutralized to swallow the identity-mismatch signal.

classes.title: Text-lab data authority / training-signal provenance corruption
classes.birth_relevance: Operator training failure class (class-kill law, 2026-07-21) cross-referenced against R1 (no external loss/reward) and R5 (one ground truth): an untraceable training-data origin means the run cannot be certified as owned-learned-signal.
classes.evidence: scripts/ember_01_custody/text_lab_data_authority_guard.py:verify_shard_census_authority -- the named-missing cycle-start cross-reference. The existing admission consumer (src/ember/governance/scripts/ember_01_identity/validate_identity.py, accepted_input / admission.training_input_authority) binds ONE claim per whole checkpoint at admission time; it never checks that every INDIVIDUAL shard a training cycle is about to consume carries that same authority. This guard closes that gap: given a receipted training-shard census (schema ember-training-shard-census-v1: cycle_id + a non-empty list of shard_id/authority_id/input_id triples) it fails closed unless EVERY shard's authority_id and input_id exactly equal the live accepted-training-input-authorities-v1.json registry's active CURRENT_EXECUTABLE authority -- reusing validate_identity._pinned_accepted_training_input() directly (never a reimplementation) so this guard can never drift from what the production admission consumer accepts. Regression suite tests/ember_01_custody/test_text_lab_data_authority_guard.py (16 tests, zero live lab data -- census fixtures are synthetic shard-source declarations, not real training shard bytes): all-shards-bound-to-active-authority accepted; a single stale/mismatched/missing authority_id or input_id on any one shard REJECTED naming that shard; empty shard list and malformed census schema REJECTED (never vacuously accepted); live-registry round-trip through the file-driven CLI entry point (cycle_start_guard); and a mutation-proof test (test_authority_comparison_mutation_guard_is_load_bearing) showing a genuinely stale-authority shard is wrongly ACCEPTED if the per-shard comparison is neutralized.

classes.title: Checkpoint / shard-size resource contradiction
classes.birth_relevance: Surfaced 2026-07 (issue #1012): the configured shard size (4 GiB) contradicts observed checkpoint sizing, an unresolved resource-envelope defect that can silently truncate or misallocate storage during a real run.
classes.evidence: #1012 merged c0b9219 (public master verified 2026-07-23): v5 split-shard writer + fixed 4 GiB transient scratch cap. The dependency-light test_checkpoint_scratch_cap.py guard exercises the exact ScratchCappedWriter used by checkpoint_artifacts.py and proves an over-cap write is rejected before destination bytes change. Full Torch integration remains covered by test_v5_writer_rejects_single_temp_shard_above_transient_scratch_cap and test_v5_transient_cap_breach_cleans_temps_and_retains_failure_evidence. CANARY scope: active-expert canary optimizer tensor lower bound ~3.214 GiB passes the 4 GiB cap. Sustained multi-domain ~7.151 GiB EXCEEDS it; optimizer-state splitting remains a named open pre-sustained GATE-2 precondition, while this guard keeps the contradiction fail-closed.
